title: SLI tension and trace budget playbook
content:
Purpose:
This note defines a lightweight playbook for reasoning about SLI tension (latency, error, and quality SLIs) against trace budget and query cost. It is targeted at instrumentation owners, oncall, and feature owners preparing rollouts of model/quantization changes.

High-level idea: SLI tension is the day-to-day tradeoff between the SLOs we expose to product (p99 latency, error-rate) and the observability cost we allow (trace retention, sample rate, probe frequency). When cost is bounded we need a principled way to allocate trace budget to routes, experiments, and cold-cache probes.

Core principles:
- Signal-first: measure the minimum set of signals needed to localize regressions within 3 hops of the causal stack (client -> router -> model shard). Avoid collecting full request bodies by default.
- Budgeted sampling: allocate a global trace budget (spans/day) and split by route importance, rollout state (canary vs global), and feature flags.
- Graceful degradation: define fallback sampling modes (full -> header-only -> headless metrics) triggered automatically when cost or query volume exceeds thresholds.
- Owner accountability: every metric/widget/trace anchor must have an owner in the signal registry.

Recommended trace budget allocation (example):
- Global baseline: 10k traces/day per region (operator baseline).
- Production critical routes (payment, billing, enterprise API): 40% of budget split across them with weighted sampling by request rate.
- Rollouts / canaries: reserve 15% of budget for active rollouts; prefer event-based full traces for regression windows.
- Experiments/PRs: 5% ad-hoc allocation with short TTLs.
- Cold-cache probing / KV warmers: 20% assigned to periodic probes to track prefix-warmth and cold-start latencies.

Sampling strategy patterns:
- Probabilistic + deterministic tail-upgrade: baseline probabilistic sampling (e.g., 0.5%) and deterministic full traces for p99 outliers and error flags.
- Session-affine sampling: keep tracing sticky per session for N minutes after an anomaly to simplify session reconstruction.
- Feature-flag tagging: traces belonging to a flagged rollout get a higher sample rate automatically.
- Adaptive sampling for KV cache: increase trace rate when KV eviction ratio increases above threshold; use low-frequency synthetic probes otherwise.

Metric definitions and compact SLI set (minimal working set):
- request.latency.p99_ms: end-to-end TTF token-first + inference service processing.
- inference.kv_cache.hit_rate: percentage of prefix hits in GPU-local KV store (window: 5m).
- route.errors.per_1000: 1k-normalized error counts (all statuses except 200/2xx).
- model.fallback_rate: fraction of requests routed to cheaper/compatible model variant due to capacity or cost policies.
- prompt.rewrite.quality: periodic eval score vs golden prompts (daily sample).

Dashboard slimming heuristics (notes for widget authors):
- Surface eight micro-SLIs per route at most: latency quantiles (p50, p95, p99), kv-warmth, error rate, cost-per-1k-tokens, fallback rate, traffic rate.
- Use compact heatmaps for latency slices instead of >10 time-series charts. Heatmaps compress long tail behavior well.
- Annotate rollouts, config changes, and model swaps with vertical lines; link to PR/Jira in panel description.
- Replace noisy raw-token-cost traces with aggregated per-route cost buckets (binned by request size) to reduce cardinality.

Investigation playbook (quick steps):
1) Check routing & fallback panel — did traffic hit a variant?
2) Inspect kv_cache.hit_rate and eviction spikes in last 15 minutes.
3) Look for correlated deployment markers (model rollout, infra scaling events).
4) If p99 spike: retrieve deterministic p99 traces (our sampling should have captured) and validate where latency accumulated (client, router, model).
5) If traces insufficient, temporarily raise trace rate for affected route and kick a synthetic probe run.

Alerting guidance:
- Alert on SLI slope (rapid increase in p95/p99) rather than absolute p99 to avoid fat-finger noise.
- Create a separate alert when trace cost approaches 80% of budget to trigger sampling-mode fallback automation.

Operational automation ideas (to iterate):
- Automated trace-throttle: when trace-cost > threshold, downgrade sampling for low-importance routes and add short lived sampling tokens to oncall for manual increase.
- Canary ticket augmentation: link canary runs to trace budget reservation so new rollouts automatically get a defined slice.
- Cost-aware dashboard modes: toggle between "operator" (detailed traces + widgets) and "product" (compact SLIs) view to reduce unnecessary query load.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Agree on global trace budget (finance + SRE input needed).
- Implement deterministic p99 trace capture: design trace anchors and minimal payload schema.
- Define owner roster for top 25 routes and assign budgets.
- Create cost model for trace retention tiers (7d vs 30d vs 90d) to drive TTLs.

Appendix (practical snippets and notes):
- Minimal trace schema: {trace_id, route, sample_reason, time_ms_buckets, error_flags, kv_hit_bool, model_variant} (store as header-only by default).
- SLO toy example: route X wants p95 < 300ms, error_rate < 0.5%; budget allocation: route X gets 1200 traces/day + 10 synthetic probes/hour.
- Slack wiring: create #obs-trace-budgets and configure automatic alerts when budget consumption crosses bands (60%, 80%, 95%).

If reviewers agree, next actions:
- schedule 30m sync with SRE and finance (owner: Maya) to finalize numeric budget and cost model (target by 2025-09-10).
- prototype deterministic p99 anchor in the tracing shim (PR assigned: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-playbooks/pull/92).
- roll out signal ownership registry entries for top 25 routes (owners to be assigned in next sprint).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the playbook lean. We don't need full fidelity everywhere; most wins are from better sampling policies and clear ownership.
- Keep an eye on KV-probe noise during holidays — synthetic probes can amplify cold-cache signals if misconfigured.

End of note.
